query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: hardware_component_type
per_column.rationale: Identifies which class of hardware (printer, network_device, etc.) is driving incidents; a candidate cause whose distribution could explain the spike. Surfaced from data, not query.

per_column.name: hardware_failure_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The mechanism (connectivity_loss, device_unresponsive) is a candidate cause of the incident spike; an alternative treatment characterizing what type of failure occurred.

per_column.name: incident_recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurrence (recurring_device_class, persistent_malfunction) sits on the path between an underlying fault and the observed count spike -- it is a manifestation/mediator of incidents inflating, not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: severity_implied
per_column.rationale: Severity characterizes the incidents themselves; it is an attribute/descriptor of the outcome rather than an independent cause or confounder of the spike.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician assignment is a downstream consequence of an incident being opened (and its type/severity), not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome. Adjusting for it would be a mistake.

per_column.name: caller_segment
per_column.rationale: User type (regular_user vs itil_user) plausibly affects both the kind of hardware/failure exposure (treatment) and the propensity to report incidents (outcome), so it is a common cause worth adjusting for.

per_column.name: location_scope
per_column.rationale: Location/scope (workstation, server_infrastructure, network_area) can drive both which hardware/failure mechanism is present (treatment) and the volume of incidents (outcome), acting as a genuine common cause.

judge.rationale: The added columns clearly supply candidate TREATMENTS (hardware_component_type, hardware_failure_mechanism) whose distributions could attribute the spike, none of which are named in the query. On confounders, two variables (caller_segment, location_scope) are plausible common causes of both the treatment (what hardware/failure is present) and the outcome (incident volume), and both were surfaced from the data rather than named in the query -- these demonstrate the capability under test, though their strength as classic common causes is only moderate. However, several columns are mislabeled risks: incident_recurrence_pattern is a mediator/manifestation of the outcome, assigned_technician is a collider (downstream of the incident), and severity_implied is an outcome descriptor. There is no true temporal/time-window confounder or baseline-load variable, which weakens the causal setup. Overall the treatment side is met and there is genuine (non-query-copied) confounder reasoning, but roughly half the columns are outcome-descriptors, mediators, or colliders rather than confounders, keeping confounder_quality moderate.
